title: What If an Earthquake Built the Tallest Dam on Earth? It Did, and 5 Million Live Below It

scenes.text: What if an earthquake built the tallest dam on Earth? It did. Nobody can take it down.
1911, the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan. An earthquake drops half a cubic mile of mountain into a valley, burying a village.
The rubble stands about 600 meters high, taller than any dam ever built. The river behind it has nowhere to go.
Over the decades it fills into Lake Sarez: 60 kilometers long, over 500 meters deep, 17 cubic kilometers of water.
If the dam ever failed, a worst-case flood could run 2,000 kilometers downriver and reach more than five million people.
Engineers judge collapse extremely unlikely, so instead of draining it, they built an alarm. Since 2004, sensors watch it day and night.

description:
What if an earthquake built a dam? In 1911 an earthquake in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan sent about 2 cubic kilometres of rock into the Murghab valley, burying the village of Usoi. The landslide dam stands roughly 600 metres high, the tallest dam on Earth, natural or man-made, according to the US Geological Survey.
Behind it Lake Sarez grew to 60 kilometres long, more than 500 metres deep and about 17 cubic kilometres of water. A worst-case outburst flood could reach more than five million people along 2,000 kilometres of river, though specialists judge a collapse extremely unlikely, and a World Bank-funded monitoring and early warning system has watched the dam since 2004.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The bigger fear is not the dam breaking but another landslide falling into the lake and sending a wave over the top. Which natural time bomb should we run through next? Drop your own what-if below.
